intro: The cabinet in the back corner of the arcade has been unplugged since 1987, but it still hums with the future; its high-score table glows while the initials keep changing. The regulars do not touch it. They say the initials arrive like missed calls, three letters at a time, and nobody has ever caught a hand in the dark. At the counter, the cashier keeps a cardboard rack of score sheets for that one machine, each ruled into two narrow columns; on every line she writes only two small figures, then adds her own initials in pencil. The sheets are always kept in order, although the order is never spoken aloud.
echo: If it didn't work, you blew on the contacts and tried again.

puzzles.title: Extra Life
puzzles.flavor: It never travels in a straight line, and neither does the truth. Start from the end; that's where it started.

blocks.text: The knight sets out from d7: Nb8 Na6 Nb4 Nc2 Na3 Nb1.

partials.a13d59bd73b3a7a74e4685b3762e4b0ff85aba52: You've decoded it, but it's not finished. One more layer.

hints: Those are chess moves. Which squares does the piece land on, and what's written there? And if what you get still isn't a word, reread the flavour text.
Start on the given square, play each move, and read the letter on every square it lands on. Then one more layer: Read what you get backwards.

puzzles.title: High Score
puzzles.flavor: The labels in the arcade have faded.
hints: Every gap takes exactly one letter. Is there a pattern in what you filled in?
Read the letters you supplied, in order.

puzzles.title: Boss Rush

blocks.text: HSLE ESP NZFCTPC NLCCTPO HLD YZE RZWO ZC DPNCPED MFE L DTYRWP HZCO OZYVPJVZYR

hints: Try moving every letter the same distance. How far turns the short words into English?
A Caesar shift: find the one shift that fixes a short word, then apply it everywhere.

puzzles.title: Player Two
puzzles.flavor: Nothing is missing. Nothing is where it was.
hints: Each word is complete but shuffled. Start with the shortest ones: does a sentence appear?
Unscramble each word where it stands; the sentence tells you what to submit.

puzzles.title: Up Up Down Down
puzzles.flavor: Walk the fence; don't read it.

blocks.text: WATEO RECRI DANTO DRERT BTSNL WRTKN HTHCU IRARE WSOGL OSCES UAIGE ODOE

hints: All the right letters are here, just out of order. Could they have been written along a path that goes up and down?
Rail fence: written in a zigzag over a few rows, then copied out row by row. Try two to five rows.

meta.title: Meta: Insert Coin
meta.flavor: The porter only ever noted where each passenger boarded.
hints: Every entry has two numbers. What in this round is numbered, and what could the second number count?
The first number picks a puzzle; the second picks a letter inside its answer.
